$description: High Contrast Light — the black-and-white twin of the main light theme, and the light member of the WCAG-AAA 'high-contrast' family. The inversion of high-contrast-dark.json: fully monochrome off the achromatic core.mono ramp, with the emphasis ladder flipped so that on a light canvas the *darkest* tone is the loudest (an alarm is near-black, a healthy reading mid-gray). No hue survives anywhere — status, diffs and the ANSI palette all separate by lightness on top of the glyphs and labels the consuming surfaces draw. AAA gates against bg.primary (#f2f2f2), via validate.py's own contrast_ratio(): text.primary 18.76:1 (>=7), text.secondary 11.29:1 (>=7), text.muted 5.13:1 (>=4.5), accent.base 18.76:1 (>=4.5), accent.on 21.00:1 on accent.base (>=7).

primary.$description: The canvas sits one step off pure white so white panel cards read as raised against it — the main light theme's grey-canvas/white-card structure, in monochrome. Anchors every AAA gate below.

muted.$description: 5.13:1 vs bg.primary — the lightest ramp step that still clears the AAA 4.5:1 floor.

base.$description: Black is the accent: on a light canvas, emphasis is maximum darkness. 18.76:1 vs bg.primary.

light.$description: The hover/secondary accent shade — a step off black so a hover state is still felt without hue.

on.$description: Foreground for text/icons on accent.base fills (e.g. primary buttons). 21.00:1 on black.

amber.$description: The decorative secondary-accent group; monochrome here, sitting one emphasis tier below accent.* so surfaces that pair the two still read as two tiers.

status.$description: The monochrome emphasis ladder, darkest = most urgent on a light canvas: error (black) > warning > success (mid-gray). Consuming surfaces carry the glyph and label that name the state; this only sets how loudly it is drawn.

default.$description: A solid ramp step rather than an alpha composite (matching the light themes' convention) — strong enough that panel edges survive on a near-white canvas.

tint.$description: Every tint family composites the same pure black, because monochrome means the accent/amber/error/success/neutral washes differ only in strength, never in hue.

error-dialog.$description: The error dialog's halo goes black with the rest of the palette — a deeper drop than any other dialog, which is what marks it as the error one.

diff.$description: Additions read dark, deletions read faint — the only distinction a monochrome diff can carry beyond the +/- gutter the renderer already draws.

ansi.$description: The 16 ANSI slots spread across the dark half of the mono ramp: program output that colors itself still separates into distinct tones, it just separates by lightness instead of hue. The bright-* slots sit one to two steps darker than their normal twins, capped at pure black.

chart.$description: Plots follow the theme: white paper, black-at-10% grid, and a 6-slot categorical palette that separates by lightness. A monochrome categorical palette tops out around six legible steps on this canvas — a plot needing more series should carry markers or dashes, not more grays.

theme.$description: No dedicated high-contrast highlight.js theme is vendored; reuses the light family's asset name (contract-tested against src/osprey/interfaces/vendor_manifest.json). Syntax highlighting is therefore the one surface this theme does not make monochrome.
